name: Tomato Bath
summary: A Karnataka-style tomato rice prepared with sona masuri rice, fresh ginger and garlic.

items: 1 standard cup sona masuri rice (0.75 rice cup)

preparation: Rinse 1 standard cup sona masuri rice (0.75 rice cup) and soak it for 20 minutes.
Chop 3 medium ripe tomatoes (about 300 g), slice 1 medium onion (about 120 g), grate 1 inch ginger and finely chop 5 garlic cloves.
cookingMethod: Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a pressure cooker. Add 1 teaspoon mustard seeds and 1 teaspoon cumin seeds; allow them to splutter.
Add 1 medium sliced onion (about 120 g), 1 inch grated ginger and 5 chopped garlic cloves. Sauté until the onion softens.

Add 3 chopped tomatoes (about 300 g), ½ teaspoon turmeric powder, 1 teaspoon red chilli powder, 1 teaspoon garam masala and salt as required. Cook until the tomatoes soften and the oil begins to separate.
Drain and add the soaked 1 standard cup sona masuri rice (0.75 rice cup). Mix gently for 1 minute.
Add 2½ standard cups water (1.875 rice cups). Build pressure on the induction cooktop, then reduce to 100°C / 300 W for 10 minutes. Allow the pressure to release naturally.
Fluff gently and finish with the juice of 1 small lemon.
servingSuggestions: Serve hot with onion-cucumber raita, plain curd or papad.
notes: This is the initial website version and can be replaced with the fully finalized chat version after review.
The standard cup conversion used throughout Shukudu Kitchen is 1 standard cup = 0.75 rice cup.

name: Vangi Bath
summary: Karnataka-style brinjal rice with capsicum and vangi bath powder.

items: 1⅓ standard cups sona masuri rice (1 rice cup)
250 g small round purple brinjal, sliced

preparation: Rinse 1⅓ standard cups sona masuri rice (1 rice cup).
Slice 250 g small round purple brinjal, 100 g capsicum and 1 medium onion (about 120 g). Keep the brinjal in water until needed to prevent discolouration.
cookingMethod: Cook 1⅓ standard cups sona masuri rice (1 rice cup) with 3⅓ standard cups water (2.5 rice cups). Build pressure, reduce to 100°C / 300 W for 10 minutes and allow natural pressure release. Spread the cooked rice gently so it does not become mushy.
Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a wide kadai. Add 1 teaspoon mustard seeds, 1 teaspoon urad dal, 1 teaspoon chana dal and 10 curry leaves.
Add 1 medium sliced onion (about 120 g) and sauté until softened.
Add 250 g sliced brinjal, 100 g sliced capsicum, ¼ teaspoon turmeric powder and salt as required. Cook covered until the brinjal is tender while retaining its shape.
Add 3½ tablespoons vangi bath powder and mix on low heat for 1–2 minutes.
Add the cooked rice gradually and fold gently until evenly coated.
Turn off the heat and finish with the juice of 1 small lemon.
servingSuggestions: Serve with plain curd, cucumber raita or potato chips.
notes: This version uses 250 g brinjal and 100 g capsicum.
Add lemon only after turning off the heat, especially when the vangi bath powder tastes slightly flat or old.

name: Curd Rice
summary: Soft, cooling curd rice designed for a small portion and a very soft texture.

items: ⅓ standard cup sona masuri rice (0.25 rice cup)
½ standard cup thick curd (0.375 rice cup)
¼ standard cup milk (0.1875 rice cup)

preparation: Rinse ⅓ standard cup sona masuri rice (0.25 rice cup).
Finely chop ½ teaspoon ginger, 1 green chilli and 1 tablespoon coriander leaves.
cookingMethod: Add ⅓ standard cup sona masuri rice (0.25 rice cup) and 1⅓ standard cups water (1 rice cup) to the pressure cooker.
Build pressure on the induction cooktop, then reduce to 100°C / 300 W for 10 minutes. Allow natural pressure release. The rice should be very soft.
Mash the hot cooked rice thoroughly. Allow it to cool until warm.
Mix in ¼ standard cup milk (0.1875 rice cup), ½ standard cup thick curd (0.375 rice cup) and salt as required.
Heat 1 teaspoon oil. Add ½ teaspoon mustard seeds, ½ teaspoon urad dal, ½ teaspoon chopped ginger, 1 chopped green chilli and 6 curry leaves.
Pour the tempering over the curd rice and mix in 1 tablespoon chopped coriander leaves.
servingSuggestions: Serve at room temperature with pickle, pomegranate or grated carrot.
notes: The 1:3 rice-to-water ratio is intentional because the rice must become very soft for curd rice.
Add a little more milk or curd before serving if the rice thickens after resting.
